# An exact obstruction to a naive Minty rank stratification

This is an obstruction to an auxiliary regularization argument, not to
surface midpoint repair or OC. A parallel body has a Lipschitz Gauss map,
but its almost-everywhere differential rank need not equal the codimension
of the actual support-face direction space.

Choose a closed nowhere-dense set E subset (0,1) of positive Lebesgue
measure. Such a fat Cantor set may be constructed by removing from each
remaining interval centrally placed open intervals with total removed
length less than one. Its complement meets every nonempty interval in
a nonempty open interval and hence in positive measure.

Define

    f'(x)=integral_0^x 1_(E^c)(t)dt,
    f(x)=integral_0^x f'(s)ds,       0<=x<=1.

Then f is C^(1,1), f''=1_(E^c) almost everywhere, and f' is strictly
increasing: the integral of 1_(E^c) over every nontrivial interval is
positive. Consequently f is strictly convex. Also 0<=f<=1/2.

Let

    B={(x,y):0<=x<=1, f(x)<=y<=2},
    K=B times [0,1] subset R^3.

This is a full-dimensional compact convex body. On its lower cylindrical
patch write

    X(x,s)=(x,f(x),s),       0<x<1, 0<s<1,
    n(x)=(f'(x),-1,0)/sqrt(1+f'(x)^2).

Because f is strictly convex, the exposed face with normal n(x) is exactly

    {(x,f(x),s):0<=s<=1},

a one-dimensional segment. This holds for every 0<x<1, not merely almost
everywhere.

The surface area on the patch is sqrt(1+f'(x)^2) dx ds. Therefore
E times (0,1) carries positive surface measure. At almost every x in E,
f''(x)=0, and hence n'(x)=0. Moreover the Lipschitz strictly monotone map
f' sends E to a set of one-dimensional measure zero, by the one-dimensional
area formula. Thus n(E) has H_1 measure zero, while the surface-area
normal marginal assigns it positive mass.

Now use the parallel/Minty parameter

    U(x,s)=X(x,s)+n(x).

This belongs to the boundary of K plus the Euclidean unit ball and has
outer normal n(x). Projection back to K sends U to X and is Lipschitz;
the coordinates x,s are Lipschitz functions of X. Thus U is a bi-Lipschitz
parameterization of this patch. At almost every x in E,

    partial_x U=(1,f'(x),0),
    partial_s U=(0,0,1).

The parameterization has rank two and positive area Jacobian there, but
the derivative of its Gauss map is zero in both parameter directions.
Its Gauss-map rank is therefore zero on a set of positive parallel-body
surface measure. The actual support faces still have dimension one.

In particular the asserted formula

    face dimension = (d-1) - rank(D Gauss map)

would give two instead of one on that positive-measure set. Neither the
Lipschitz projection from the parallel body nor C^(1,1) regularity fixes
this discrepancy. A decomposition using only differential ranks cannot
silently be substituted for a decomposition by actual convex faces.

The conditional surface law along each generator in this example is
uniform in s. The example is therefore itself straightforwardly
repairable by its product geometry. Its purpose is to rule out the
specific rank inference and motivate the separate conditional-ball
localization proof, which uses no such stratification.
